entries.name: run_command
entries.label: run a command
entries.description: Run one bash command line on this Linux machine as the user and return its output. The user sees the exact command and must approve it before it runs. Everything the command starts ends with it: a backgrounded process does not outlive the call. Use search_files, read_file, system_facts or hyprctl instead when one of them fits.

command.description: the exact command line, bash syntax, as typed at a prompt

entries.name: search_files
entries.label: search files
entries.description: Search file CONTENTS with a regular expression (case-insensitive), anywhere on this machine, hidden files included. Returns path:line:text, at most 20 hits per file, lines cut at 240 characters. Machine-generated trees (caches, package stores, build directories, agent transcripts) are not searched. Default path is ~, but when the user names a place pass `path`: searching all of ~ is slower and noisier than the directory they meant, and may hit the 20 s limit. Use it before read_file when you do not know where something is.

path.description: directory or file to search; default ~

glob.description: only files matching this glob, e.g. *.qml

entries.note: hidden files and ignore-listed files are searched (--hidden --no-ignore: ~/.config is where this shell lives, and neither ~/.claude nor ~/.cache is in a git repo, so --no-ignore costs nothing and dropping it costs 186 s). MACHINE-GENERATED TREES ARE PRUNED, and that is what makes a search of ~ finish: .cache, .local/state, .local/share, node_modules, .claude, .venv, __pycache__, .npm, .rustup, .cargo/registry, target, build -- plus .git and /proc /sys /dev /run. Measured 2026-09-11 on this machine, pattern Theme\.surface over ~: without them 20 s, killed (exit 124), 186 138 bytes of which the 32 KB that reached the model held 0 lines from the directory the user asked about; with them 2.8-13.7 s over five runs, exit 0, 82 lines, 9 217 bytes, every one real. --max-columns-preview shows the head of a long line instead of the bare marker "[Omitted long matching line]" (111 of 215 lines were that marker). --max-filesize 4M is the belt for a stray blob inside a tree we keep. Errors such as permission denied are silent (--no-messages). When ripgrep is absent the fallback argv is: grep -rnIE -i --color=never -m 20 --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.cache --exclude-dir=state --exclude-dir=share --exclude-dir=.claude --exclude-dir=.venv --exclude-dir=__pycache__ --exclude-dir=.npm --exclude-dir=.rustup --exclude-dir=target --exclude-dir=build --exclude-dir=proc --exclude-dir=sys --exclude-dir=dev --exclude-dir=run [--include={glob}] -e {pattern} -- {path=~}
entries.retryHint: narrow it and call again: pass `path`, or a `glob`, or a tighter pattern

entries.name: read_file
entries.label: read a file
entries.description: Read the start (head) or the end (tail) of one file on this machine as text, up to max_bytes (default 65536). The trailer says whether the file was cut. Use search_files first when you do not know the path.

max_bytes.description: how many bytes from the start; default 65536

head.description: the first max_bytes of the file

max_bytes.description: how many bytes from the end; default 65536

tail.description: the last max_bytes of the file (a log's newest lines)

entries.name: clipboard_read
entries.label: read the clipboard
entries.description: Read the text on the Wayland clipboard. A clipboard that holds no text is exit 1 (no text on the clipboard).

entries.name: clipboard_write
entries.label: put text on the clipboard
entries.description: Put text on the Wayland clipboard, replacing what is there. The user sees the text in full and must approve.

text.description: the exact text to place on the clipboard

entries.name: screenshot
entries.label: take a screenshot
entries.description: Take a screenshot of the whole screen (mode full) or let the user select a region (mode region; they may cancel). The picture is given to you as an image right after this tool's result. Nothing on the machine changes.

entries.name: fetch_url
entries.label: fetch a web page
entries.description: Fetch one http(s) URL and return its text (HTML reduced to text, scripts and styles dropped), at most 2 MB in 20 s. The user must approve: a URL can carry data off this machine.

entries.name: notify
entries.label: show a notification
entries.description: Show a desktop notification with a title and an optional body. The user must approve.

entries.name: write_file
entries.label: write a file
entries.description: Write text to one file on this machine, creating or overwriting it (the parent directory is created). The user sees the resolved path (symlinks followed) and the whole content and must approve, so do not repeat the content in your answer afterwards unless asked. Reports the byte count and sha256 written.

entries.name: calculator
entries.label: do arithmetic
entries.description: Evaluate one arithmetic or math expression exactly (Python syntax: + - * / // % **, parentheses, comparisons, and math.* functions such as math.sqrt, math.log, math.sin; abs round min max sum len int float). Use it for any calculation instead of doing arithmetic in your head.

entries.name: web_search
entries.label: search the web
entries.description: Search the web through this machine's own SearXNG instance, a local metasearch server that asks a set of public engines and merges their answers (no API key, no account, one host to trust). Returns any direct answer first, then numbered results as title, URL and a one-line snippet, with the engines that found each one. Use it for anything you do not know or that may have changed since you were trained, and fetch_url afterwards to read a result in full. The query itself leaves this machine.

query.description: the search query, as words rather than a question

count.description: how many results to return; default 8
